controls.summary: Keep a created task launch-pending until an authoritative full task observation confirms its state; omission from a partial or limited list is not failure evidence.
evidence: A limited task-list response omitted an active issue #60 Luna task.
A subsequent full task-list response confirmed the task was active in its generated worktree.

controls.summary: Check model authority before any mutation and stop all orchestration, protected planning or governance work unless the active model is Sol Extra High.
evidence: Protected orchestration design began while the active model was Terra Medium.
Repository model governance permits Terra to read protected planning but forbids it from materially creating, editing, approving, or restructuring that planning.

controls.summary: Capture operational lessons automatically as local candidates, but adopt durable controls only through evidence, an issue, Sol Extra High approval, tests, and a protected pull request.
evidence: Chat memory did not reliably preserve prior task-launch semantics.
Repository-owned controls can be validated and applied by every future task and heartbeat.

controls.summary: Advance a launched implementation only after its authoritative task record proves the requested model, generated worktree and exact accepted base SHA.
evidence: A task creation requested a commit before the protected remote-tracking ref had been fetched locally.
The successful issue #60 task was confirmed only after a full task observation exposed its real task ID and generated worktree.

controls.summary: Before dependent delivery, prove live GitHub connector, exact SSH refs, credential-safe CLI reads and an authenticated protected write path; record each action class and keep browser authentication explicitly user-controlled.
evidence: Installed GitHub plugin files remained present while the live connector disappeared from a prior task, so installation metadata did not prove mounting.
Repository ownership, public reads and SSH pushes succeeded while the stored CLI credential was denied issue updates and pull-request mutations.

controls.summary: Treat merge as non-terminal: require exact trusted target-branch validation, issue acceptance and closure evidence, every declared parent outcome, and milestone or wave re-evaluation before reconciliation or dependent delivery.
evidence: The delivery state previously made merged terminal and represented neither trusted target-branch validation nor issue and parent reconciliation.
Closed Wave 3 child issues retained unchecked acceptance criteria while parent epic #22 remained entirely unchecked with no roll-up evidence.
The repository default branch is main while ordinary delivery targets develop, so closing keywords did not replace explicit integration-branch reconciliation.
Protected PR #93 passed planning governance, unit, integration, exact-image browser, CodeQL and dependency review before this ledger adoption.

controls.summary: Derive agent authority from declared pipeline tiers rather than hardcoded model names, and accept one planning attestation per authority including an explicit human-owner value.
evidence: The orchestration validator asserted single-model equality for orchestration, protected planning and implementation, so a second pipeline could not be admitted without editing validator source.
The planning gate accepted one hardcoded model attestation, leaving no truthful attestation for Claude-authored or human-authored protected planning while forbidding false attestation.
A Claude review of the authenticated sign-in flow found and fixed an exploitable open redirect under issue 110, evidencing independent review value from a second pipeline.
controls.retirementReason: ADR-0009 restores Sol-only orchestration and replaces peer pipelines with qualification-gated implementation routing.

controls.summary: Require a reconciled delivery to itemise every acceptance criterion with its own evidence, so a reviewed-complete claim is auditable rather than asserted from memory.
evidence: The v1.1 wave plan was held only in conversation, contradicting the repository-is-source-of-truth rule in AGENTS.md.
Issue 118 was reported complete while three of its own acceptance criteria were unmet, because completion was judged from remembered scope rather than the recorded issue.
The prior check accepted a single self-asserted acceptanceChecklist enum with closure evidence unlinked to individual criteria.

controls.summary: Justify wave concurrency by reconciliation cost as well as disjoint file ownership, record the assessment per slice, and cap in-flight pull requests while the target branch requires up-to-date branches.
evidence: Five pull requests were opened concurrently on the basis of disjoint file ownership; each merge forced the remainder behind, requiring serial update-and-revalidate cycles that found no defect.
The implementation plan recorded file ownership but no reconciliation cost, presenting disjointness as sufficient grounds for concurrency.

controls.summary: Investigate a delivery failure as a fault class: identify the shape of the mistake, sweep the whole change for other instances, and correct them together rather than one validation cycle at a time.
evidence: Pull request 155 failed four times across five validation cycles on one fault class: changing an element's role or context while leaving everything that assumed the old one in place. A single sweep after the first failure would have found all four.
Issue 146 had three defects corrected one at a time, including a hypothesis that proved wrong and removed working behaviour before the real cause was found.

controls.summary: Keep orchestration with Sol Extra High and route bounded implementation by exact provider, model and task-class capability; stop evaluation by pass five, avoid heuristic session-token caps, and intervene only on task-appropriate evidence of stalled progress.
evidence: Claude produced useful bounded implementation but its temporary peer-pipeline authority resulted in project-management and governance changes that required Sol audit and repair.

Representative hidden-case benchmarks distinguished a correct Mistral Medium 3.5 High implementation from lower Mistral profiles that failed correctness checks, proving that provider name or nominal tier is not sufficient qualification.

A heuristic local token cap interrupted correct work and an administrative handback while the provider panel later reported only about EUR 0.09 used from a EUR 25.50 allowance, showing that the local cumulative-token counter did not represent billed capacity or capability.

controls.summary: Prefer the cheapest qualified idle implementation capacity, but permit the next qualified provider to take a separate ready issue when the cheaper provider is occupied and exact disjoint paths, satisfied dependencies, a material throughput benefit, bounded revalidation and the two-pull-request cap are evidenced.
evidence: Strict provider serialization left independently paid and qualified implementation capacity idle even when a separate ready issue could progress without overlapping files or changing the active task's premises.

ORCH-009 showed that five concurrent pull requests created repeated rebase-and-revalidation waste, so beneficial provider concurrency retains the existing cap of two in-flight pull requests and sequential Sol integration.

Mistral Medium 3.5 High produced the correct bounded architecture for issue #185 while independent governance work proceeded on disjoint paths, demonstrating useful throughput without transferring orchestration or integration authority.
